newsitem.title: USA: NE Ill. planning $34.2 bln for transit thru 2020.
newsitem.headline: NE Ill. planning $34.2 bln for transit thru 2020.

text.p: A northeastern Illinois transportation plan calls for spending more than $34.2 billion for maintenance, rehabilitation and additions to the system through 2020, a report outline released Tuesday states.
Most of the spending, about $27.7 billion, is earmarked for maintaining and rehabilitating the existing system, according to the outline which was released by Chicago Area Transportation Study.

The plan also provides about $5.1 billion for three new expressways, a new commuter rail line in the suburban Chicago area, a new elevated train line in Chicago and extensions to roads and rail transit lines.
Another $440 million of spending has been allocated for arterial roads connecting to expressways and $760 million to enhance commuter rail, elevated rapid transit and bus services.
Local suburban bus services have been provided $50 million for improvements and non-motorized traffic $175 million to improve access and encourage usage.
The Regional Transportation Plan Committee is to release the plan to the public on Monday.
More than 500 projects were submitted for possible inclusion and 20 have been selected for funding, said Maureen Mullady, public involvement coordinator for the Chicago Area Transportation Study.
Another 20 projects that did not make the list have been selected for consideration if funding becomes available, Mullady said.
